page.overview:
Who is Alfredo Pián?

= Alfredo Pián = Alfredo Pián (21 October 1912 – 25 July 1990) was an Argentine racing driver who briefly competed in Formula One during its inaugural season in 1950. Though his career at the top level was cut short by injury, he remained a respected figure in Argentine motorsport during the mid-20th century.

Pián was born in Las Rosas, Santa Fe Province, Argentina, into a family with strong mechanical and engineering interests. From an early age he was fascinated by automobiles, beginning his racing career in the flourishing national motorsport scene of Argentina in the 1930s and 1940s. During this period, road racing was highly popular, and Pián built a reputation as a skilled and determined driver in long-distance competitions.

Before his involvement in international competition, Pián achieved success in Argentine racing, including national-level events and the Turismo Carretera category. His performances gained him recognition among the leading South American drivers of the time, alongside names such as Juan Manuel Fangio and José Froilán González.

In 1950, Pián was given an opportunity to compete in the newly established Formula One World Championship. He was entered for the 1950 Monaco Grand Prix as a privateer driving a Maserati 4CLT, managed by Scuderia Achille Varzi. During Saturday practice, however, Pián lost control of his car on the harbour front section of the circuit. He crashed heavily into the guardrail and was thrown from the car, suffering serious leg injuries.
